subtype: Approach: choosing by brand name alone [Pitfall]
passage: When Lokesh's offer letter came from the famous IT company, his father distributed pedhas to the whole lane in their town near Sangli. Relatives called from three villages. Nobody asked what the job was, and Lokesh didn't either. The other offer, from a small agri-tech firm in Kolhapur that built soil-testing tools, he declined in one line. Six months later, home for Gudi Padwa, Lokesh sat on the verandah with his school friend Yogesh. "So, what do you do there?" Yogesh asked. Lokesh paused. "I watch server alerts. When one turns red, I raise a ticket for another team." "And then?" "Then the next one turns red." Yogesh was quiet. "The Kolhapur people came to our village last month. They're testing soil for my father's farm." Lokesh looked at the pedha in his hand and didn't eat it.

qa.q: What does Lokesh not eating the pedha suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Lokesh felt regret and a quiet sadness, seeing that the famous name brought pride to others but dull work to Lokesh.

qa.q: What would you change first if choosing again?
qa.a: Ask each company exactly what the role involves day to day and what you would learn, before letting the name decide.

qa.q: How might Yogesh see Lokesh's job?
qa.a: Yogesh sees past the famous name to repetitive work, and his mention of the Kolhapur firm hints at what Lokesh gave up.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate taking the famous company for the family's pride without checking the role, and finding the work repetitive with little growth.
